text.p: Pfizer Inc said on Monday it "remained comfortable" with Wall Street forecasts for its 1996 full-year earnings in the $2.90-to-$3.00 range.
First Call listed the consensus estimate for the pharmaceutical company's 1996 profits at $2.98 a share.
Pfizer reported third quarter earnings of $0.80 a share, up from $0.67 a year ago and topping forecasts of $0.79 a share.
Its stock was up 1-5/8 to 83 in afternoon trading.
Pfizer said its third quarter pharmaceutical sales rose 13 percent to $2.04 billion.

Its Norvasc cardiovascular drug had sales of $471 million in the quarter, up 41 percent over 1995's third quarter. An older-line heart drug, Procardia XL, saw its sales drop 15 percent to $249 million due to lower prescription levels, Pfizer said.
Among other drugs, the anti-infective Zithromax had third quarter sales of $124 million, up 83 percent over a year ago. The anti-depressant Zoloft grew 27 percent to $350 million.

Zyrtec sales jumped 967 percent to $36 million, up from $4 million a year ago. The allergy drug, licensed in the U.S. and Canada by Pfizer from Belgium's UCB SA, was cleared for marketing in the U.S. in December.

Pfizer had total sales of $2.80 billion in the quarter, up from $2.54 billion a year ago. Exchange rate fluctuations reduced total dollar sales by 4.4 percent, Pfizer said. Price had no major impact on sales in the quarter, it said.
Analysts had expected the strong U.S. dollar to cut into drug companies' sales figures by lowering international sales in dollar terms.
